chapter_theme: Two songs at Vazhuvur (வழுவூர்): a plea to be kept from women and Death and given true knowledge and the shade of the feet, and a song of thanksgiving recalling, stage by stage, the poet's initiation: teaching, Tamil, light, nada and the peacock's coming.
structure_note: 809 is a plea in the usual two halves; 810 replaces the plea with remembrance (மறவேனே), listing what the Lord has already done.

809.reading: The poet asks not to sink in the sea of unending infatuation with cuckoo-voiced deceitful women, nor to have Death, fiery-eyed, with noose and trident, cloud-black on his buffalo, come near; and that, with the sins of this impure body since the womb, its sorrow, desire and deceit, and his poverty ended, true knowledge, ripened awareness and love of Siva come, and the shade of the anklet-bearing feet be given. The praise shows Murugan on the new peacock with Indra's daughter on one side and the hunters' deer on the other, the twelve-armed hero with civet and rosewater garlands and the sacred thread, son of Siva the Mahadeva and Sadasiva, at the old town of Vazhuvur of cool tanks, groves and paddy, known for its great penance.
809.nuance: The plea moves from two dangers to avoid (women, Death) to a list of gifts: போதம், மெய்ஞானம், சிவநேசம். கருவூறிய நாளும் ... மல தேகம்: the body is impure from conception. மிடி (poverty) is named among the ills to end, beside sin and desire.

810.reading: The poet recalls what the Lord did: on the first day made him praise the feet with love, fed him the meaning of the teaching, bathed him in the sea of mantra, penance and knowledge, joined him to his company, fed him the three Tamils the gods do not know, showed the Veda's path, showed the light of the kala circling the mandala, raised him to the nada beyond the light, set him at the doorstep of the fragrant whorl, leapt over fate, brought him to Kamalalaya and the open space, and then came lovingly mounted on the radiant peacock; he will not forget it. The praise names the vel that felled the hill and the demons' heads, Murugan who fed Siva, Sivakami's rogue lover with serpent garlands, the meaning of Siva-knowledge, Valli's husband, and the lord of Vazhuvur where the gods praise his dance.
810.nuance: A rare autobiographical song: the plea is replaced by remembrance (செயல் மறவேனே), and the stages read as an inner ascent: teaching (உபதேசப் பொருள்), Tamil (முத்தமிழ்), the light of kala (கலை சோதிக் கதிர்), nada (நாதப் பரம்), the whorl (சுழி), the space (வெளி). கமலாலைப் பதி may be Tiruvarur, whose tank is Kamalalayam, or the lotus within; I cannot settle it. சிவகாமிக்கு ஒரு தூர்த்தர் is a playful epithet of Siva.

links.note: 809 asks that Death, fiery-eyed with noose and trident on his buffalo, not come near (சமனார் ... அணுகாதே) and that true knowledge (மெய்ஞானம்) and love of Siva be given. Tirumular says that if Yama comes he will strike him with the sword of knowledge (நமன்வரின் ஞானவாள் கொண்டே எறிவன்). The knowledge 809 asks for is the weapon Tirumular claims to hold, so the plea and the boast describe the same remedy from either side.

810 recalls how the Lord led him through the teaching, the light of the kala (கலை சோதிக் கதிர்), nada and the whorl until he entered the open space (வெளியாகப் புக). Tirumular says that by gracious Nandi he knew the space and the light in its middle, and beyond that knows nothing (வெளியை அறிந்து வெளியின் நடுவே ஒளியை ... செழுநந்தியாலே). Both tell a guru-led passage through light to space in the first person; Arunagiri adds Tamil and nada to the stages.
